Question: All sides of the convex pentagon \(ABCDE\) are of equal length, and \(\angle A=\angle B=90^\circ.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle E?\)
Solution:
Join \(C\) to \(E\) to separate the pentagon into a quadrilateral and a triangle. The right angles at \(A\) and \(B\) make \(AE\) and \(BC\) perpendicular to \(AB\). Convexity puts \(E\) and \(C\) on the same side of \(AB\). Since \(AE=BC=AB\), these segments form the square \(ABCE\).

The square gives \(CE=AB\) and \(\angle AEC=90^\circ\). All pentagon sides are equal, so \(CD=DE=CE\). Thus triangle \(CDE\) is equilateral, and \(\angle CED=60^\circ\).

Because the pentagon is convex, diagonal \(EC\) lies inside the interior angle \(AED\). Therefore
\[
\angle E=\angle AEC+\angle CED
=90^\circ+60^\circ=150^\circ.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{150^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
